component.name: Notav
component.summary: Notes and a journal kept in your Nextcloud

description.p: Notav keeps your notes as plain Markdown files in your Nextcloud, so the Nextcloud Notes app and Obsidian can open the same folder.

ul.li: Works offline; changes sync when the server is reachable
Notes edited on two devices at once are both kept
Folders, search, and a Markdown editor
Connects through GNOME Online Accounts or a browser sign-in
Notes kept as Markdown files in a folder of your Nextcloud Files (Notes/ by default, as the Nextcloud Notes app), synced over WebDAV; Notav works from a local copy, also offline
Sign-in through GNOME Online Accounts, the browser, or a login name and app password, then the notes folder to use
The notes folder as a tree of folders and notes in the sidebar, as in Obsidian
Search through titles and text, ignoring case and accents
Markdown editor that saves as you type, styled for reading: headings sized by level, the Markdown marks dimmed, a line of about 80 characters; the title renames the note
Drag notes and folders into and out of folders in the sidebar
Sidebar menu (right click): new note or folder inside a folder, next to a note, or at the top level; delete a note
A note changed on two devices at once keeps both versions: yours as a conflict copy next to it
A note locked on the server (open in Nextcloud Text) waits with its change and the rest syncs; the app says who locked it and since when, and can unlock it
Preferences: style, notes folder (moving the notes there or not), account, settings sync
About has a Support page with where to support Notav's development: Ko-fi, GitHub Sponsors and Liberapay
An RPM spec for Fedora, built on COPR from .copr/Makefile; Notav uses the system's SQLite
